hints: For the least value of $P$, the particle is on the point of slipping down the plane, so limiting friction $F = \mu R = 0.4R$ acts up the plane.
Resolve forces perpendicular to the plane to express normal reaction $R$ in terms of $P$: $R = P\sin 35^\circ + 0.6g\cos 35^\circ$.
Resolve forces parallel to the plane to form $F + P\cos 35^\circ = 0.6g\sin 35^\circ$.
Substitute $F = 0.4R$ and solve the linear equation for $P$.
walkthrough:
To find the least value of $P$ to maintain equilibrium, recognise that the particle is on the verge of sliding down the incline. Therefore, friction acts up the plane at its maximum limiting value:
$$F = \mu R = 0.4R$$

Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane (taking outwards as positive):
$$R - P\sin 35^\circ - mg\cos 35^\circ = 0$$
$$R = P\sin 35^\circ + (0.6)(10)\cos 35^\circ = P\sin 35^\circ + 6\cos 35^\circ$$

Resolve forces parallel to the inclined plane (taking up the slope as positive):
$$P\cos 35^\circ + F - mg\sin 35^\circ = 0$$
$$P\cos 35^\circ + F = 6\sin 35^\circ$$

Group terms containing $P$ on the left-hand side and numerical terms on the right-hand side:
$$P(\cos 35^\circ + 0.4\sin 35^\circ) = 6\sin 35^\circ - 2.4\cos 35^\circ$$

Divide to find the least force $P$:
$$P = \frac{1.475494}{1.048582} \approx 1.40713\text{ N}$$
$$P = 1.41\text{ N}\quad (\text{to 3 significant figures})$$
